item.title: UK Government Guidance - Money Laundering Advisory Notice - October 2026 - HM Treasury Advisory Notice: Changes To The Financial Action Task Force’s Public Lists
item.content:encoded:
The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 (“the MLRs”) require the UK regulated sector to apply enhanced customer due diligence in relation to countries identified as high-risk jurisdictions by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF). This obligation is in addition to the requirement to apply enhanced customer due diligence where there is an assessed high risk of money laundering or terrorist financing, including geographic risk based on credible sources (for example the UK’s National Risk Assessment).

Regulation 33(1)(b) of the MLRs requires regulated businesses (“relevant persons”) to apply enhanced customer due diligence measures and enhanced ongoing monitoring in any business relationships with a person established in a FATF call for action country or in relation to any relevant transaction where either of the parties to the transaction is established in a FATF call for action country, where a FATF call for action country is defined as a country named on the FATF’s list of “High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call to Action”.

For these purposes, regulation 33(3) explains that:

  • a relevant transaction means a transaction in relation to which the relevant person is required to apply customer due diligence measures under regulation 27;
  • being established in a country means:
    • in the case of a legal person, being incorporated in or having its principal place of business in that country, or, in the case of a financial institution or a credit institution, having its principal regulatory authority in that country; and
    • in the case of an individual, being resident in that country, but not merely having been born in that country.

In order to keep abreast of which countries are FATF call for action countries, relevant persons should refer directly to the list published by the FATF of “High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action”. This list is updated three times a year, on the final day of each FATF Plenary meeting, held every February, June and October. The dates of these meetings are published several months in advance, in the events calendar on the FATF website. The FATF lists of countries are updated and published in full, and can be found via the High-risk and other monitored jurisdictions page on the FATF website. Please see below a copy of the current jurisdictions on these lists.

Applying Enhanced Due Diligence on new and existing customers established in high-risk third countries

Regulation 33(1)(b) requires businesses to apply enhanced customer due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring in any business relationship with a person established in a FATF call for action country or in relation to any relevant transaction where either of the parties to the transaction is established in a FATF call for action country. This means that relevant persons are obliged to carry out enhanced customer due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring on all customers, new and existing, established in FATF call for action countries. Relevant persons should refer to their sector-specific guidance, approved by HM Treasury, for further advice on meeting their obligations under regulation 33.

Group wide controls

Regulation 20(3) requires relevant persons to ensure third-country branches and subsidiaries in countries with weaker AML/CTF requirements than the UK apply measures equivalent to those in the UK. Regulation 33(1)(b) and 20(3) taken together create a requirement for UK relevant persons to ensure any of their branches or subsidiaries based in FATF call for action countries apply measures equivalent to the enhanced customer due diligence measures set out in regulation 33(3A) that the branch or subsidiary would be required to implement were they based in the UK.

When considering what measures are necessary to fulfil these obligations, firms should also consider where customers of branches or subsidiaries have already been subject to measures equivalent to enhanced due diligence as a result of increased geographical risk in line with regulation 33(6)(c).

The Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Regulations 2026

On 30 June 2026, the Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Amendment) Regulations 2026 (‘the amendment regulations’) took effect. Regulation 19 of the amendment regulations amended the previous requirement in regulation 33 of the MLRs for enhanced due diligence on “high risk third countries”. Enhanced due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring is now only required for business relationships with a person established in a jurisdiction listed by FATF as a High-Risk Jurisdiction subject to a Call for Action or in relation to relevant transactions where either of the parties to the transaction is established in a jurisdiction listed by FATF as one of the High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action.  

Relevant persons continue to be required to take FATF mutual evaluations into account as a relevant geographical risk factor in line with regulation 33(6)(c) and must apply enhanced due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring where they identify a high risk of money laundering or terrorist financing.

FATF public statement

On 30 October 2026, the FATF published the most recent update to its lists of jurisdictions identified as having strategic deficiencies in their AML/CTF regimes, of “Jurisdictions Under Increased Monitoring” and “High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action”.

Inclusion on FATF’s list of Jurisdictions Under Increased Monitoring does not, of itself, trigger the requirements in regulation 33(1)(b), but remains relevant to the assessment of geographical risk under regulation 33(6)(c).

  • Angola
  • Bolivia
  • Bosnia and Herzegovina

  • Bosnia and Herzegovina

Background Information

1. This advice replaces all previous advisory notices issued by HM Treasury on this subject.

2. The Financial Action Task Force is an inter-governmental body established by the G7 in 1989 and today includes as members 38 jurisdictions and two regional organisations (the European Commission and the Gulf Co-operation Council). It is the global standard setter and monitoring body for anti-money laundering and counter terrorist financing.

3. The Government’s strategy is to use financial tools to deter crime and terrorism, detect it when it happens, and disrupt those responsible and hold them to account for their actions. The FATF is central to the UK’s international objectives within this strategy.

4. The Money Laundering, Terrorist Financing and Transfer of Funds (Information on the Payer) Regulations 2017 require firms to put in place policies and procedures in order to prevent activities related to money laundering and terrorist financing. Regulated businesses are also required to apply enhanced customer due diligence and enhanced ongoing monitoring on a risk-sensitive basis in certain defined situations and in any other case which by its nature can present a higher risk of money laundering or terrorist financing.

5. Other restrictive measures are applicable in the UK in respect of some of the jurisdictions listed in the content of this advisory notice.

6. Further information about what HM Treasury is doing to combat financial crime, and how to subscribe to financial crime alerts.

item.title: ADI Foundation And The Vault Partner To Strengthen Institutional Custody Technology And Advance Post-Quantum Security On ADI Chain
item.content:encoded:
• The Vault will bring its multi-party computation custody technology to ADI Chain and lead joint research into quantum-resistant security, as tokenized real-world assets reach a record US$32.1 billion globally.

ADI Foundation, the organization behind the institutional blockchain network ADI Chain, and The Vault, an institutional digital asset infrastructure platform, have announced a strategic partnership to strengthen digital asset custody infrastructure and advance research into post-quantum security.

As financial institutions increasingly adopt stablecoins and tokenized real-world assets, technology that secures these assets against both current and emerging threats is becoming a critical requirement. The value of tokenized real-world assets reached a record US$34 billion in September 2026, while the total stablecoin market stood at US$313 billion. The partnership brings together ADI Chain's institutional blockchain infrastructure and The Vault's expertise in digital asset custody technology and advanced cryptography to strengthen the security infrastructure supporting institutional participation in on-chain financial markets.

Under the partnership, The Vault plans to integrate ADI Chain into its institutional custody platform, enabling support for the ADI token and assets issued on the network, including DDSC, the UAE dirham-backed stablecoin. Once implemented, the integration is intended to allow institutions using The Vault's platform to manage supported ADI Chain assets through established security controls, transaction authorization policies and multi-party computation (MPC) technology.

The Vault will also make its custody infrastructure and proprietary MPC technology available to ADI Foundation. Its technology distributes transaction-signing authority across multiple parties, reducing reliance on any single individual or device to authorize asset transfers. The Vault's cryptographic library has undergone independent security review by Halborn.

The partnership will also explore post-quantum security to help protect digital assets against future threats from quantum computing. The Vault will lead research into quantum-resistant signing technology for MPC wallets, building on ML-DSA, a cryptographic standard published by the US National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). ADI Foundation will contribute expertise on integrating these capabilities with ADI Chain, with the goal of strengthening the long-term security of institutional digital assets.

Andrey Lazorenko, CEO of ADI Foundation, said:

“Secure custody is a fundamental requirement for bringing institutional finance on-chain. As stablecoins and tokenized assets become more widely adopted, institutions need confidence that their assets can be securely managed and protected over the long term. Our partnership with The Vault strengthens the infrastructure supporting ADI Chain today, while helping us explore the next generation of security capabilities needed for institutional digital finance.”

Artem Stopnevich, CEO of The Vault, said:

"The UAE has been one of the earliest jurisdictions to put regulated digital money into real use, and networks such as ADI Chain are being built to carry it at institutional scale. As a technology provider, our role is to give institutions robust control over how their digital assets are held, managed and transferred, with the same confidence they place in the traditional financial system, today and in ten years' time. Bringing our MPC custody technology to the ADI ecosystem addresses the first part of that, and our post-quantum research with ADI Foundation is how we intend to prepare for the challenges of the quantum era."

The partnership will also include joint technical research, industry engagement and ecosystem development initiatives to support institutional adoption of ADI Chain.

The organizations plan to establish a joint working group to define the custody integration timeline and post-quantum research roadmap, with further milestones to be announced as the collaboration progresses.

item.title: FSB Recommends Türkiye Further Strengthens Its Regulatory Framework For Crypto-Assets And Stablecoins
item.content:encoded:
• Peer review finds Turkish authorities have made meaningful progress in enhancing the regulation, supervision and oversight of crypto-assets.
  • Further steps are warranted to reinforce Türkiye’s framework and improve alignment with the FSB Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-asset Activities.
  • The FSB recommends Türkiye operationalises a financial stability monitoring framework, establishes a regime for stablecoins, strengthens supervision and enforcement, and promotes cross-border cooperation and information sharing.

The Financial Stability Board (FSB) today published its second Peer Review of Türkiye, examining the country’s progress in implementing the FSB recommendations for the regulation and supervision of crypto-asset activities, including stablecoins.

Since the publication of the Thematic Review on the FSB Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-asset Activities in 2025, the Turkish authorities have made meaningful progress in strengthening the regulation, supervision and oversight of crypto-asset markets and activities. Authorities have brought a large part of the crypto-asset market within the regulatory perimeter, introducing registration and licensing requirements for crypto-asset service providers (CASPs). Moreover, structural safeguards, such as strict custody separation, and the prohibition on the use of crypto-assets for domestic payments, limit some of the risk transmission channels into payments and banking.

This regulatory framework allows authorities to better understand the business models of CASPs and the channels through which financial stability risks could arise. Authorities have also operationalised a centralised data platform for monitoring crypto-asset activities.

However, further steps are warranted to reinforce the country’s regulatory framework and improve alignment with the FSB Global Regulatory Framework for Crypto-asset Activities.

Building on these achievements, the FSB recommends that Turkish authorities further enhance crypto-asset and stablecoin regulation and supervision by operationalising a framework for financial stability monitoring, establishing a dedicated regime for stablecoins, strengthening supervision and enforcement, and promoting effective cross-border cooperation and information sharing.

Background

At the G20’s request, the FSB has led international work on the financial stability risks of crypto-assets since 2018. In July 2023, it finalised a global regulatory framework made up of two sets of recommendations: one for crypto-asset activities and markets, and a revised one for global stablecoin arrangements. The FSB’s 2025 thematic peer review found welcome progress in putting the framework into practice, but also highlighted significant gaps and inconsistencies across jurisdictions, and called on them to prioritise full and consistent implementation.

FSB member jurisdictions have committed to undergo periodic peer reviews to evaluate their adherence to international financial standards. To fulfil this responsibility, the FSB has established a regular programme of country and thematic peer reviews of its member jurisdictions. As part of this commitment, Türkiye volunteered to undergo a peer review in 2026. A schedule of country peer reviews, as well as all completed peer review reports, are available on the FSB website.

The FSB coordinates at the international level the work of national financial authorities and international standard-setting bodies and develops and promotes the implementation of effective regulatory, supervisory, and other financial sector policies in the interest of financial stability. It brings together national authorities responsible for financial stability in 24 countries and jurisdictions, international financial institutions, sector-specific international groupings of regulators and supervisors, and committees of central bank experts. The FSB also conducts outreach with approximately 70 other jurisdictions through its six Regional Consultative Groups.

The FSB is chaired by Andrew Bailey, Governor of the Bank of England. The FSB Secretariat is located in Basel, Switzerland and hosted by the Bank for International Settlements.

Publication

11 November 2026

Peer Review of Türkiye

Peer review assesses Türkiye’s progress in implementing the FSB recommendations for the regulation and supervision of crypto-asset activities, including stablecoins.

item.title: This Morning, Representatives Of The Hedge Fund Association (IHFA) Opened Trading On The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange
item.content:encoded:
This morning (November 11, 2026), the CEO and board members of the Israel Hedge Fund Association (IHFA) opened trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) in a opening  bell ceremony marking the the Association's 13th Annual International Conference.

More than 100 hedge fund managers from Israel and abroad attended the ceremony, including CEOs and founders of some of the largest and most influential hedge funds in the world. Their participation reflects the importance of the linkage between the Israeli investment industry and the international financial community. Alongside senior industry figures, new immigrants from the investment field who chose to join the Israeli industry also took part.

The ceremony was accompanied by Agam Berger, a former hostage in captivity, playing the violin in a moving moment that carried a message of unity, hope and faith in a better future.

After the ceremony, the 13th Annual International Conference of the Association opened at the TASE conference center, with hundreds of representatives from the hedge fund industry and from the Israeli and international capital markets. Participants included managers of local and international hedge funds, institutional investors from Israel and abroad, representatives of multi-family offices, law and accounting firms, local and foreign banks, investment houses, trustees, administrators and other professionals in the industry.

The conference was opened by Bank of Israel Governor Prof. Amir Yaron, with a lecture on "The Israeli Economy – Challenges and Opportunities".

Natalie Raz, CEO of the Israel Hedge Fund Association, said: "The hedge fund industry in Israel continues to develop, innovate and create value, even in a complex economic and security reality. Today, about 260 hedge funds operate in Israel, managing together about NIS 65 billion. The industry relies on professional human capital, knowledge and experience, and is an important part of the development of the Israeli capital market.

We see great importance in deepening ties and cooperation with the global hedge fund industry. The participation at the conference of managers of leading funds from around the world, alongside professionals who chose to immigrate to Israel and join the local industry, reflects the growing connection between Israel and the world's investment centers, and the confidence in the ability of the Israeli hedge fund industry to continue to develop, renew itself and grow.

Hedge funds bring to the capital market expertise, managerial flexibility and diverse investment strategies. They contribute to the development of an advanced capital market, to encouraging innovation and to job creation. I believe that the continued development of the industry is of great importance for strengthening the Israeli capital market and expanding financial activity in Israel.

We are proud of the Israeli hedge fund industry and of the people who lead it. We will continue to work in cooperation with the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and with all parties in the capital market to advance initiatives that will strengthen the industry and contribute to the growth and resilience of the Israeli economy."

Ittai Ben Zeev, TASE : "The current period requires, more than ever, deepening the cooperation between TASE and the hedge fund industry. The funds are key partners in developing the Israeli capital market and connecting it to international markets, thanks to the expertise, diverse investment strategies and connections they bring with them. Over the past year, the TASE has become more attractive to international investors, among other things following the successful transition to trading Monday through Friday, in line with the standard accepted in global markets. Deepening the relationship with hedge funds in Israel and abroad is an essential part of expanding the participation of international investors in the local capital market, broadening the investor base and deepening liquidity. We view the hedge fund industry as a long-term partner, and we will continue to work together to strengthen the Israeli capital market and deepen its connection to international markets."

In the photo: Natalie Raz, CEO of the Israel Hedge FundAssociation; Max Krapel and Lior Segev, representing the Association's board members; Agam Berger, a former hostage in captivity; Ittai Ben Zeev, CEO of the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, and members of the Association's board.

item.title: Western Exchanges Surge As Emerging Market Venues Slump In October: FTSE Mondo Visione Index

Global exchange stocks split sharply in October 2026, with performance determined by geographic footprint and asset specialisation, according to the FTSE Mondo Visione Exchanges Index.

Western exchanges lead

  • Cboe Global Markets topped the sector with a 21.9% return in USD terms. 
  • It was followed by:- London Stock Exchange Group: +17.4%
  • MX Group: +16.9%
  • CME Group: +15.7%
  • Nasdaq: +15.5%

Investors favoured platforms with strong derivatives clearing businesses and recurring data subscription income.

Emerging markets and Asia lag

  • Brazil's B3 SA was the weakest performer, down 30.2%. Others posted steep falls:
  • Boursa Kuwait: -10.8%
  • Singapore Exchange: -10.1%
  • Dubai Financial Market: -9.4%

Shifting institutional capital flows and weaker local currencies hit venues that rely mainly on cash-equity trading.

The FTSE Mondo Visione Index closed October at 104,360.3 points, up 8.7% from its September close of 95,998.56. It set a closing all-time high of 105,656.17 on 30 October 2026.

item.title: DIP Holding Debuts On DFM As The UAE’s First IPO For 2026
item.content:encoded:
• The IPO attracted strong demand from local, regional and international investors.
  • The offering raised AED 1.9 billion (USD 529 million), implying a market capitalisation of AED 9.7 billion (USD 2.6 billion) at listing, with shares priced at AED 1.12 per share.
  • DIP Holding’s listing brings an established infrastructure-like ground rent and services platform to DFM.

Dubai Financial Market (“DFM”) today welcomed the successful debut of DIP Holding PLC (“DIP Holding” or the “Company”), the owner of Dubai Investments Park (“DIP” or the “Park”). The listing marks the UAE’s first initial public offering (IPO) in 2026, underscoring confidence in the UAE and Dubai’s capital markets and position as a leading global investment hub.

The IPO raised approximately AED 1.9 billion (USD 529 million) through the sale of 1,735,243,300 existing ordinary shares, representing 20% of the Company’s issued share capital, by Dubai Investments PJSC, the sole selling shareholder, which retains an 80% stake following the listing.

The IPO was priced at AED 1.12 per share, implying a market capitalisation of approximately AED 9.7 billion (USD 2.6 billion) at listing and an implied dividend yield of approximately 7.5% based on the Company's expected annualised dividend of AED 725 million in respect of FY2027. The Offering attracted strong demand from local, regional and international investors, with strong coverage across the previously announced price range.

To mark the listing, Khalid bin Kalban, Chairman of DIP Holding and Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dubai Investments PJSC and Omar AlMesmar, Chief Executive Officer of DIP Holding, rang the market-opening bell at DFM in the presence of His Excellency Helal Al Marri, Chairman of the DFM Board of Directors and Hamed Ali, Chief Executive Officer of DFM and Nasdaq Dubai. They were joined by Board members, senior management and employees from Dubai Investments and DIP Holding, alongside Al Mal Capital, financial adviser to Dubai Investments on the IPO and representatives of the banks, bookrunners, legal advisers and other transaction partners who supported the successful completion of the Offering and listing.

Khalid Jassim Bin Kalban, Chairman of DIP Holding and Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dubai Investments PJSC, said: “Today is an incredibly proud moment for both DIP Holding and Dubai Investments. The successful completion of this IPO and Dubai Investments’ first partial exit through a public offering, represents an important milestone in the Group’s journey and demonstrates its ability to build, scale and bring to market strong, mature and resilient businesses. The strong appetite that has been seen from a broad mix of investors is a clear endorsement of DIP Holding’s differentiated business model, the quality and stability of the business that has been built over more than 25 years, and the strength of Dubai Investments’ approach to long-term value creation. It is also a powerful vote of confidence in Dubai, its growth story and the continued depth and attractiveness of its capital markets. The Group is grateful to all the new shareholders for the confidence they have placed in DIP Holding and particularly pleased to see Dubai Investments shareholders participate in the offering and continue on this next chapter of the company’s journey.”

Omar AlMesmar, Chief Executive Officer of DIP Holding, said: “Today is a moment of immense pride for everyone at DIP Holding and DIP Holding is incredibly excited to begin this next chapter as a publicly listed company. DIP Holding enters the market from a position of strength, with a differentiated capital-light business model that delivers stable, recurring income, supported by long-term leases and a highly committed tenant base that has invested significantly in the Park over the years. The exceptional performance in the first half of 2026 demonstrates the strength and resilience of the business, and this shows significant opportunities to build on this momentum. With clear and visible growth levers through embedded rental repricing, increasing subleasing fees and the repositioning of plots to higher-value uses, DIP Holding is confident in its ability to deliver sustainable earnings growth and strong cash generation, without the need for significant additional capital investment. DIP Holding is delighted to welcome its new shareholders alongside Dubai Investments and looks forward to rewarding their confidence as it builds on the strong foundations, executes its growth strategy and unlocks the full potential of DIP Holding in the years ahead.”

His Excellency Helal Al Marri, Chairman of the DFM Board of Directors, said: “The debut of DIP Holding, as the UAE’s first initial public offering of 2026, signals renewed conviction among issuers and investors alike in the strength and direction of Dubai’s capital markets, where total market capitalisation on DFM has reached over AED 1 trillion. Guided by the vision of His Highness Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance, we continue to widen access to equity markets for established national companies and to bring new income-generating asset classes within reach of investors. Each new listing strengthens Dubai’s standing as a financial centre of choice for companies seeking international capital.”

Hamed Ali, Chief Executive Officer of DFM and Nasdaq Dubai, added: “The listing of DIP Holding reflects the strength of demand in Dubai markets, with the offering attracting strong interest from local, regional and international investors. It also introduces a distinctive, income-generating profile to DFM, underpinned by long-term leases and a committed tenant base. As we continue to strengthen our market infrastructure and widen the opportunities available to investors, our focus remains on supporting companies well beyond listing day.”

In line with its dividend policy, DIP Holding expects to distribute annualised cash dividends of AED 700 million for FY2026, excluding the AED 100 million pre-IPO dividend distributed in September 2026, followed by AED 725 million for FY2027 and AED 750 million for FY2028. The first post-IPO distribution of AED 350 million, relating to the full second half of 2026, is expected to be paid in April 2027.

The Company’s shares commenced trading today under the ticker symbol “DIP” and ISIN “AEE02089D257”. The listing comes amid a period of increased trading activity and continued institutional participation in Dubai’s capital markets. As of September 2026, total market capitalisation on DFM stood at AED 993 billion. Total traded value increased by 22% year-on-year to AED 162 billion during the first nine months of 2026, while average daily traded value rose by 25% to AED 883 million.

item.title: Deutsche Börse Group Offers 24/7 Global Trading For Tokenized DAX 40 Equities On 360X
item.content:encoded:
• xStocks brings the DAX 40 onchain, opening Germany’s largest listed companies to 24/7 global trading on 360X.
  • Tokenized shares of all 40 DAX constituents arrive as part of an xStocks expansion into UK- and EU-listed equities, building on Payward’s strategic partnership with Deutsche Börse Group.
  • Tokenized versions of SAP (SAPx), Siemens (SIEx), Allianz (ALV.DEx), Deutsche Telekom (DTE.DEx) are available from day one.

Tokenized DAX 40 equities are now available on 360X, an affiliated company of Deutsche Börse Group, alongside Xetra-Gold as an xStock. This opens up onchain distribution for Europe's largest gold security with physical backing. In addition to the recently announced 24/7 trading of DAX 40 equities, it extends distribution to digital-native investors.

xStocks, the tokenized equities framework developed by Payward, has deployed tokenized equities representing every constituent of the DAX 40, Germany’s benchmark stock index. The launch brings onchain the 40 largest blue-chip companies listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange and puts them within reach of investors in more than 110 markets. The exchange is operated under Deutsche Börse Group, Payward’s strategic partner. 

Each xStock is backed 1:1 by the underlying share, held by a regulated custodian, and tradable 24/7 across select venues. Tokenized versions of SAP (SAPx), Siemens (SIEx), Allianz (ALV.DEx), Deutsche Telekom (DTE.DEx) and others are available from day one. For many investors around the world, this expansion is the first practical way to gain exposure to German capital markets. It also gives the companies themselves a new distribution channel into a global pool of onchain investors, whose demand feeds back to the underlying shares.

“German companies have a track record of building innovative products which the whole world relies on, yet there are investors on every continent who have been restricted from investing in these companies,” says Mark Greenberg, Payward’s Chief Commercial Officer. “Bringing the DAX 40 fully onchain through our work with Deutsche Börse Group breaks that barriers, allowing someone in Southeast Asia or Latin America to finally hold tokenized Siemens or Allianz from the same wallet they already use, and trade whenever they like, including the hours when Frankfurt is asleep.”

“Our partnership with Payward is exactly the kind of collaboration that accelerates the transformation of capital markets,” says Carlo Kölzer, Head of FX and Digital Asset at Deutsche Börse Group and Co-CEO of 360X. “Our vision is to provide a unified hybrid exchange ecosystem – delivering seamless trading on- and off-chain across traditional and tokenized assets, bridging deep centralized liquidity with interoperable settlement.”

Deutsche Börse Group and Payward have partnered on several initiatives since December 2025 as part of a broader agreement to combine regulated infrastructure with crypto-native expertise and deliver frictionless institutional access. xStocks already trade on 360X, the Deutsche Börse-backed venue regulated under the EU’s DLT Pilot Regime since February 2026.

xStocks launched in June 2025, initially as tokenized representations of U.S. stocks and ETFs, proving that permissionless, onchain and 24/7 markets could unlock global distribution channels for assets to be held, transacted and deployed across DeFi from anywhere in the world. The framework has since grown to span more than 1,300 xStocks, representing tokenized stocks, ETFs and early access to IPOs, the widest range of assets offered by any tokenized equities framework. It has also grown to include more than US$1 billion in assets under management, with more than US$45 billion of total transaction volume and more than 500,000 unique holders worldwide.

item.title: Sharegain’s Keren Halperin Re-Elected To ISLA Board
item.content:encoded:
Sharegain, the global leader in securities lending for retail-facing financial institutions, today announced that Deputy CEO Keren Halperin  has been re-elected to the Board of Directors of the International Securities Lending Association (ISLA) for a second consecutive term.

For over 20 years, Keren’s career has been rooted in capital markets, as a trader at a

pioneering algo-trading firm, later as a regulator in the legal department of a major stock exchange, and for the past decade, Deputy CEO of Sharegain. Keren’s re-appointment is a recognition of this unique blend of experience and the broad perspective it has given her on the securities lending market.

The International Securities Lending Association is the leading trade association for the securities financing industry, with 280+ global members based in 35 jurisdictions, including beneficial owners, investors, asset managers, custodians, lenders, prime brokers and service providers, spanning the breadth of the securities financing ecosystem.

ISLA works with its members, global regulators and policy-makers, to drive clarity and best practice in a rapidly evolving landscape. The fifteen Officers and Directors on the ISLA board, who represent a geographically and functionally diverse group of member firms, work closely with ISLA’s senior management team to ensure that its strategy meets the demands of its growing membership and of society more broadly.

Commenting on her re-election, Keren said:

“Securities lending is experiencing exceptional growth, driven by factors including new sources of supply, developing markets and increased retail participation – with digital assets and tokenization reshaping how securities and collateral move. I will continue to champion this growth, bringing the voice of new participants and the next generation of beneficial owners from the neo-brokers and trading platforms I work with every day.

“I am equally committed to nurturing rising talent, advancing an equitable industry, and extending ISLA’s global footprint, so the brightest minds see our sector as the place to build an innovative, human-centric career.

“I would like to thank ISLA’s members for their continued trust. It’s a privilege to serve alongside such a talented and committed Board.”
